clue.text: French painter read novel at home

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or fresh, so the letters of read take a new order

parts.note: at home is IN, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone at home is reading a novel about a French artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book being read but signals the anagram: READ becomes DERA, then IN follows. André Derain was a Fauvist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: André Derain was a Fauvist artist from France, a contemporary of Matisse.

clue.text: Mythical monster and continental fish

parts.note: a dragon is the fire-breathing monster of myth
et is French, a continental language, for the word and

explanation.surface: A list pairs a legendary beast with a fish from mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' looks like it describes the fish, but it turns 'and' into French ET.
explanation.definitionFit: The dragonet is a small, brightly coloured bottom-dwelling sea fish.

clue.text: Rap minder getting confused?

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so rap and minder are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A minder is muddled about what a rap means.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: RAPMINDER rearranges into the answer, and a rap is itself a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap is a sharp rebuke, and a confused rap is still a telling-off.

clue.text: Herriot always included a small amount

indicators.note: included says the letters sit inside the run of the words Herriot always

explanation.surface: The vet-author James Herriot always put a little something in.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across HerrIOT Always. James Herriot wrote the Yorkshire vet stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota, the smallest Greek letter, is used for a tiny quantity, a jot.

clue.text: Scott's senior monk

explanation.surface: A novelist's head of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott wrote a novel with this title, and the head of an abbey is its chief monk.

clue.text: Female call could be a catch

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A woman's phone call might be worth catching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' suggests catching a call, but it means a fish landed by a fisherman.
explanation.definitionFit: Herring are fished in large numbers, so one is a typical haul for a trawler.

clue.text: A sign of being possessive?

parts.note: reads as jealousy, but means the punctuation mark that shows possession in grammar, as in the cat's

explanation.surface: Someone shows the first hint of jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: In writing, the possessive case is marked by this raised comma before an s.

clue.text: I go into farm building to collect child

indicators.note: going into something puts a piece inside another

parts.note: a barn is a farm building for storing crops

explanation.surface: Someone heads into the barn to fetch a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRN is the Scottish and northern English word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scots word for a young person or baby.

clue.text: Nurse upset about offer

parts.note: to nurse is to tend, look after

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word about is read bottom to top

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A nurse is upset about a job offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reads as distressed, but it turns RE to ER after TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to present formally, as in tendering a bid or resignation.

clue.text: Going up to get a clue

parts.note: a scent is a trail or lead, as in hounds on the scent

explanation.surface: A climber goes uphill to find a hint.
explanation.walkthrough: A scent is a clue, as in a detective being on the scent.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb, the act of moving upward.

clue.text: Cooked pie — repast before another meal?

definitions.text: Cooked pie — repast before another meal?

indicators.note: cooking changes ingredients into a new form, so pie and repast are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A pie is baked as a snack ahead of the main dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE and REPAST shuffle into the answer, and the whole clue describes it: a small dish served before the main meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter course served ahead of the main dishes is meant to whet the hunger.

clue.text: Vegetable head

explanation.surface: A gardener's prize crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off one's onion' is British slang for crazy, the onion being the head.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bulb grown in kitchen gardens, and in slang it is one's skull or noggin.

clue.text: Leave out nothing with German

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
mit is the German for with

explanation.surface: Someone declines to join in a German venture.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to skip or exclude something.

clue.text: Opposition to Second World War movement

explanation.surface: Wartime defiance against an occupying power.
explanation.walkthrough: In occupied France the underground fighters against the Nazis were called the Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: It means pushing back against something, and it names the underground fighters in occupied Europe in the 1940s.

clue.text: Two girls acquire organ stop

parts.note: Clara is a girl's name
Bella is another girl's name

explanation.surface: A pair of young women take over the controls of an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarabella is a flute-toned pipe-organ register with a sweet sound.

clue.text: Oriental father exchanges lute for shoulder-piece

parts.note: E stands for east, so oriental
pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: exchanges means the letters of lute swap places among themselves

explanation.surface: An Eastern dad trades in his lute for a decoration worn on the shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanges' seems to mean trading the lute away, but it shuffles LUTE to ULET after E and PA.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulet is an ornamental pad on the shoulder of a uniform.

clue.text: According to Chesterton, a wicked shopkeeper

definitions.text: According to Chesterton, a wicked shopkeeper

parts.words: According to Chesterton, a wicked shopkeeper
parts.note: G. K. Chesterton's Song Against ... opens with God made the wicked ..., so the clue points to that trader

explanation.surface: A writer's view of a villainous shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue's leading '3' is an OCR stray; the page has none. The poem is in Chesterton's novel The Flying Inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's poem condemns the trader who sells food and household goods.

clue.text: It improves delivery

parts.note: delivery reads as the post or a parcel service, but means the way a speaker utters words

explanation.surface: A new system speeds up the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Training in clear, expressive public speaking makes a speaker's diction better.

clue.text: It provides 13 against heat

parts.note: 13 is the across answer meaning opposition, so the clue describes a material that opposes heat

explanation.surface: Something offers protection from heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 13 is RESISTANCE: this fibrous mineral was used for fireproofing because it withstands heat.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral fibre was widely used to fireproof buildings, being non-flammable.

clue.text: Loves new road to the east — starts striding

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of road form a fresh arrangement

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: starts means just the opening letter of striding

explanation.surface: A walker loves the fresh road heading east and sets off at a stride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROAD into ADOR; E and the S that 'starts' takes from 'striding' follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to worship or cherish them.

clue.text: Rum to see son with tent dweller

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees
a camper lives in a tent

explanation.surface: A boy dashes off to visit the camper in the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Rum', but the definition needs 'Run': a misprint of one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to scurry or dash about lightly.

clue.text: Trains swimmers?

explanation.surface: Coaching for athletes in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmers' suggests people in a pool, but fish swim in groups called schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is to educate or drill, and groups of fish travelling together are shoals of that name.

clue.text: "Jealous in honour, — and quick in quarrel" (Shakespeare)

definitions.text: "Jealous in honour, — and quick in quarrel" (Shakespeare)

parts.words: "Jealous in honour, — and quick in quarrel" (Shakespeare)
parts.note: the line describes the soldier in the Seven Ages of Man speech from As You Like It, with one adjective left blank

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare with a word to fill in.
explanation.walkthrough: On the page a dash marks the gap. Jaques's speech says the soldier is 'Jealous in honour, sudden and quick in quarrel'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective means abrupt or hasty, fitting a hot-tempered soldier.

clue.text: Holy for example

parts.note: Holy reads as sacred, but is the name of Holy, also called Lindisfarne, off Northumberland

explanation.surface: Something sacred given as an instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Holy Island, or Lindisfarne, lies off the coast of Northumberland in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lindisfarne, known as Holy, is a tidal piece of land surrounded by sea.

clue.text: I dread boss moving pieces of furniture

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters of I dread boss are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An employee fears the boss shifting the office furniture around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' seems to describe shifting furniture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideboards are long dining-room cabinets for storing crockery.

clue.text: Drugs fools

explanation.surface: Narcotics for idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for narcotics, so to dope is to drug, and a dope is an idiot.

clue.text: Certain to meet bridge player by river

parts.note: S is South, one of the four players at bridge
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A card player is sure to meet a partner down by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points, so S is South. The Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure and certain are synonyms meaning without doubt.

clue.text: A short tale so to speak

definitions.text: A short tale so to speak

parts.words: A short tale so to speak
parts.note: tale is said the same as tail, so the clue means a stubby tail, as on a rabbit or deer

explanation.surface: Someone tells a brief story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' tells you to hear 'tale' as 'tail'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a hare, rabbit or deer.

clue.text: Horrify a gentle friend

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft or gentle
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted friend could be shocked.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano) is the music marking for playing softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or dismay deeply.

clue.text: Before writing there is a rule

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before
script is handwriting or written text

explanation.surface: Before you put pen to paper, there is a rule to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescript is a decree or ordinance laid down in advance.

clue.text: Gives up hope when spread is ruined

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of spread is are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A host loses heart when the buffet is spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' reads as a buffet meal; it is just fodder for the anagram signalled by 'ruined'.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all faith that things will improve.

clue.text: Tolerates part of football ground

explanation.surface: Putting up with a section of a sports stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: One who puts up with something bears it, and the tiered seating areas at a stadium share the name.
